stemMd: An aqueous solution of a soluble metal hydroxide contains an excess of which ion relative to neutral water at the same temperature?
explanationMd: A soluble hydroxide dissociates and raises the hydroxide-ion concentration. At a fixed temperature the water ion product links hydroxide and hydrogen-ion concentrations, so increasing one lowers the other. The metal identity does not require nitrate, carbonate or chloride to be present.

distractorRationale.c: A basic solution has a lower hydrogen-ion concentration than neutral water.
distractorRationale.e: A hydroxide does not necessarily supply nitrate.
distractorRationale.b: A hydroxide does not necessarily supply carbonate.
distractorRationale.a: A hydroxide does not necessarily supply chloride.
